explanation: Fires on tokens inside quoted string literals or attribute values in code (Python/JS/HTML/PHP/CSS), e.g. the word inside '__main__', '95%', 'email', 'keywords', or a tag name after '<' inside a string. It is strongest on the content right after an opening quote in code. Quoted words in ordinary prose get weak to moderate activation.

Fires on function or method names and operators that come right before an argument list in code (.call, .isArray, len(, std::move, strncmp, === ). It also fires on relational prepositions in prose that link a head noun to its complement (of, by, on, between, in). Both look like 'operator/relation token that takes the next argument'. Sentence-final periods and ordinary content words are weak.

Fires on the '@' in academic citation markers such as '[@B9]', '([@bib29])' or '\[@ref5]', most strongly on the first citation after a sentence or an opening parenthesis. Weaker offshoots are other special symbols inside markup or template syntax ('*' in ["*"], '{%', '#' in {#sec}, '\' in LaTeX). Ordinary words are near zero.

Fires on the comma that ends a sentence-initial adverbial or introductory phrase ('Therefore,', 'However,', 'In this case,', 'In 1998,', 'Here,') before the main clause starts. Commas after mid-sentence clauses and clause-linking words (where, but, that) get moderate activation. Other tokens are weak.

Diffuse. It fires on digits inside numbers and years, variables in math expressions, URL '://', CSS class fragments, and many ordinary words in mid-sentence ('to', 'want', 'be', 'instead'). No shared token or context is visible.

A mixture. It fires on leading indentation whitespace or tabs at the start of a code line (before '{', '}' or a key), on legal-procedure verbs after a party name ('Defendant moves', 'petitioned', 'moved for', 'argues'), and on word-piece fragments in the middle of a word (piez-oe-lectric, Cambrid-ges-hire, Turb-op-rops). These do not share an obvious common feature.

Mainly fires on the '=' or '+' and the '(-' token in auto-generated arithmetic or algebra word problems ('Solve 3*g + 23 = ...', '(-44)/(-8)'). There are scattered strong hits on unrelated tokens in prose and code (namespace ';', '{', 'accredited', 'do'). Fire on math operators in these problem templates; elsewhere expect sporadic activation.

Fires on characters inside random alphanumeric ID strings, especially the first few characters after the slash in short URLs (pic.twitter.com/6..., t.co/..., jsfiddle or jsbin IDs, YouTube IDs) and in tokens or API keys. It is weak on digits in ordinary numbers or initials in names.

Diffuse. It fires on mid-sentence function words and other tokens in informal or blog prose (articles 'the' and 'a', 'is', ''s', 'like', 'for', and an opening parenthesis before an abbreviation), plus some code and number tokens. No specific trigger is visible.

Mixed. It fires on URL path segments ('/wiki', '/master', 'www'), on the whitespace or digit before a number in counts ('and 62 benign', 'and 4453'), on subscript digits in chemical formulas, and on assorted list or markup tokens. Several unrelated jobs.

Fires on fragments inside rare or technical multi-token words, especially biomedical, Latin or Greek terms and proper names (hy-g-roma, spermato-zo-a, P-aph-os, symp-athe-ctomy). It also fires on 'except' in the license boilerplate 'may not use this file except' and on 'prevent'/'ensure'/'and' in protective or pest contexts. A mixture of jobs.

Mixed. It fires on 'NOT' in 'DO NOT modify/EDIT', on sentence-initial 'Please' in notices, on 'to' after verbs and adjectives ('urged a judge to', 'conducted to', 'too pure to'), and on syllable fragments in the middle of uncommon personal names (Dou, Jer-ro-ld, D-zh-okhar, T-JO-FL). Several unrelated jobs.

Mixed. It fires on ' value' in HTML '<option value=', on digits in OIDs and decimal numbers, on 'of' in legal date phrases ('6th day of August'), and on various imperative-politeness or code tokens. No single theme.

Fires inside descriptive noun phrases with modifiers or ranges, often in formal, scientific or legal text: the connector or second element of a coordination or range ('temporary or', 'lakes and', 'aged 9 and 20', 'west of', 'city of', a comma after a place or institution name). There are scattered other strong hits (file paths, name fragments). It is only partly coherent.
